extracted.intended_audience: readers interested in research integrity, academic misconduct, whistleblowers, and science journalism
extracted.subtask_description: A journalistic/blog-post account of a high-profile scientific misconduct case that documents institutional responses, whistleblower treatment, and ethical failures in human-subjects research. Useful for readers learning how institutions, journals, and individuals should (or failed to) handle allegations of misconduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical permission for human experiments
rubrics_metrics.description: He had never obtained ethical permission to conduct his experiments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Human-subjects experiments must have prior ethical approval; failing to obtain permission is a fundamental breach (example: Macchiarini performed experimental transplants without ethical permission).

rubrics_metrics.name: Accurate reporting of clinical outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: The 2011 study in The Lancet had misrepresented the outcome of Beyene’s implant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publications must truthfully and accurately report patient outcomes; misrepresentation in journal articles constitutes scientific misconduct and damages trust in the literature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Informed consent obtained before intervention
rubrics_metrics.description: Of the three patients... only Beyene had signed a consent form—and the form was dated two weeks after his surgery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consent forms must be obtained and dated prior to interventions; post-dated or absent consent is unethical and invalidates the legitimacy of the research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection from retaliation for whistleblowers
rubrics_metrics.description: Retaliation against the whistleblowers came quickly. ... they were told that they had violated patient privacy and would be fired immediately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions should protect, not punish, individuals who raise bona fide concerns; punitive actions (formal warnings, threats of firing) against whistleblowers are an abuse and discourage reporting of wrongdoing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid reporting whistleblowers to law enforcement without basis
rubrics_metrics.description: The Karolinska Institute also reported the whistleblowers to the police. 'I was called down to the police and put in a room with no windows, with a tape recorder and a lawyer and a policeman in front of me, and interrogated.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resorting to police complaints against internal critics, especially over alleged privacy violations when anonymization and approvals were in place, can be coercive and intimidating; such steps should be justified, proportionate, and not used to silence dissent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigations should address human-subjects abuses
rubrics_metrics.description: The inquiry didn’t address any potential abuses of human subjects, but the result of the inquiry was clear. Macchiarini had falsified his research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: External inquiries into alleged misconduct must explicitly examine possible harms to human subjects and ethical violations in clinical practice, not only data or publication issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prompt, transparent institutional response to findings
rubrics_metrics.description: It took months for them to respond, and when they finally came to a conclusion, they called a press conference. 'We asked if we could attend the press conference, and they said no' ... 'they were hiring guards to stop us from attending.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions should respond in a timely manner to credible allegations and conduct transparent communications that allow affected parties to participate rather than exclude or intimidate them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not dismiss external inquiry findings without justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Accompanied by members of the Nobel Committee, Hamsten disavowed Gerdin’s external inquiry and proclaimed his confidence in Macchiarini.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutional leaders should not reflexively reject credible external investigations; decisions to disavow should be based on evidence, not institutional loyalty or reputation protection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journal editorial responsibility and avoidance of shielding authors
rubrics_metrics.description: The Lancet applauded the decision with an editorial titled 'Paolo Macchiarini Is Not Guilty of Scientific Misconduct.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journals and editors have a duty to investigate and respond appropriately to allegations of misconduct rather than protect authors; failing to do so undermines journal credibility and public trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency and inclusion in public-facing processes
rubrics_metrics.description: They then called our boss at the time and said that they were hiring guards to stop us from attending.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public events like press conferences about misconduct investigations should be open and allow stakeholders to attend or be represented; exclusion and security measures to keep critics away signal lack of transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support and mitigation for whistleblowers' personal/professional harm
rubrics_metrics.description: The stress was overwhelming. 'I mean, I couldn’t sleep. I was always thinking of this next strategic move,' ... 'People he considered friends stopped returning his calls and emails. He could not concentrate on his research. He found it hard to give his children the attention they needed.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions should provide psychological, career, and legal support to whistleblowers and take steps to mitigate reputational and professional damage that can result from raising concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adherence to ethical procedures for accessing patient records
rubrics_metrics.description: Corbascio had applied in advance for ethical permission to access patient records. 'I wrote that ethics application because I knew that they were going to try to fire us.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Those investigating or reporting concerns must follow institutional ethics and data-access procedures (e.g., prior approvals) to protect patient privacy and to ensure their actions are defensible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manage conflicts of interest and institutional bias during investigations
rubrics_metrics.description: I’m just baffled as to why the leaders of prestigious institutions so consistently defend their scientists even with such clear evidence of misconduct... 'They are not only scientists; they likely serve as managers, hold important university positions, and are deeply involved in the organizational aspects of the institution.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigative processes should identify and mitigate conflicts of interest among decision-makers (administrators, Nobel Committee members, etc.) so institutional loyalties do not override impartial evaluation of evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective enforcement and meaningful sanctions for misconduct
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Misconduct is rarely perceived. If perceived, it is not reported. If reported, it is not investigated. If investigated, violations are not found. If found, they are excused. If they are not excused, penalties are light.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Professional and institutional disciplinary systems should impose proportionate and effective sanctions when misconduct is established; light or symbolic penalties fail as deterrents and perpetuate systemic problems.
